scenario: A podcast-industry report features only language-learning shows that survive two years and grow subscribers by more than 60%. Publishers use the featured mean to estimate typical subscriber growth.

data.description: Only surviving shows with growth above 60 percentage points are featured. Growth is Normal with sigma 25 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean subscriber-growth mu across all shows and (b) the fraction of shows featured.
naive_answer: Typical growth is about 72.2 points because that is the featured average.
naive_trap: Only upper-tail surviving podcasts are featured.
reasoning_trace: Use the lower-truncated normal model with alpha around 1.2.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(60-mu)/25; return mu+25*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-72.18
mu=brentq(eq,-100,59.99)
frac=norm.sf((60-mu)/25)
assert abs(mu-30)<2 and abs(frac-0.1151)<0.005
